feedbackActionPlan.summary: Add an optional "Additional notes" field to the custom order flow so customers can provide special instructions that are reviewed by staff and included in order records and confirmations.
feedbackActionPlan.customerImpact: Customers gain a clear place to communicate non-standard details, questions, delivery constraints, or clarifications without forcing them into unrelated option fields.
feedbackActionPlan.businessImpact: Reduces follow-up messages, captures context at order time, improves handoff to production and customer service, and lowers the risk of missed custom requirements.
feedbackActionPlan.confidence: The repository checkout appears to contain a billiards physics project rather than the production website or order form, so the plan is based on product and UX implementation requirements rather than concrete code paths.

researchFindings.finding: No website, checkout, CMS, or order-management implementation surface was visible in this checkout; implementation targets are therefore described by functional area.
The raw feedback asks for a "notes or addition information" section; customer-facing copy should use the clearer label "Additional notes" or "Additional information".
The field should be optional, late in the custom-order configuration flow, and visible again on the review step before payment so customers can verify the note before submitting.
Because notes may contain special instructions but should not become an unbounded support inbox, a concise maximum length, live character counter, and helper text are needed.

implementationPlan.step: Add an optional textarea labeled "Additional notes" near the end of the custom order form, after required product configuration fields and before the order review or checkout transition.
Add helper text such as "Share special instructions or questions for this custom order. Do not include payment information."
Use a maximum length of 1000 characters, display a remaining-character counter, trim leading and trailing whitespace on submit, and treat an empty trimmed value as no note.
Allow plain text and line breaks only; escape rendered output everywhere, normalize line endings, reject or strip control characters, and do not interpret HTML, links, or markup.
Persist the note as an order-level field attached to the custom order record, not as a product option that affects pricing or inventory.
Show the note in the customer-facing review step before order submission with an edit path back to the textarea.
Include the submitted note in the customer order confirmation page, confirmation email, and customer account order-detail view when a note is present.

Expose the note prominently in admin order detail, production work order views, customer-service views, and internal notification emails; visually mark orders that contain notes so staff do not miss them.
Add audit-safe display behavior for admin users: preserve line breaks, show the full text up to the stored maximum, and include the note in order exports or print views used by production.
If the order flow has validation schemas, API contracts, email templates, or admin serializers, update each path so the note is accepted, stored, rendered, and omitted cleanly when blank.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Customers can enter an optional additional-notes value during custom order configuration.
The textarea appears after required configuration fields and before final order review or checkout submission.
The submitted value is limited to 1000 characters, trimmed, stored as plain text, and safely escaped wherever rendered.
Blank or whitespace-only notes are not shown as empty sections in customer or admin views.
A non-empty note appears on the review step before purchase, the order confirmation page, the confirmation email, and the customer order-detail page.
A non-empty note appears in admin order detail and production/customer-service workflows used to fulfill the order.
Admin and production users can distinguish orders with notes without opening unrelated configuration fields.
The field does not change price, deposit calculation, SKU selection, inventory handling, or required-option validation.

risks.risk: Customers may use notes to request changes that should affect price or feasibility; helper text and staff review are needed so notes do not bypass structured option rules.
If notes are only stored on the customer-facing order and not surfaced in production/admin views, the feature could create false confidence while staff still miss special instructions.
Unescaped note rendering could introduce cross-site scripting or email-template injection issues.
Overly long notes could clutter confirmations and admin views if no maximum length or display treatment is enforced.

openQuestions.question: Which order-management surfaces are authoritative for production: admin order detail, exported work orders, printed build sheets, or third-party fulfillment tools?
Should staff be able to edit or annotate the customer note internally after order submission, or should it remain immutable customer-provided text?
Should confirmation emails include the full note or a shortened preview with a link to the order detail?
